applies_why: This judge text evaluates the Matthew 1:16 link through the verse’s own admitted ambiguity, which is the kind of verse-level assessment K-C governs.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: either it bars resolving a link from a single verse's admitted ambiguity, or it permits verse-level underdetermination when the parties' chain answers are mentioned.
why: By making the link turn on whether a single verse admits both readings, it resolves verse by verse instead of by weighing the chains by footing as K-C requires.
